newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Torch zinc LME quality claim withdrawn - Zhuzhou.
newsitem.headline: Torch zinc LME quality claim withdrawn - Zhuzhou.

text.p: China's Zhuzhou smelter said on Monday a claim made to the London Metal Exchange (LME) that the smelter's Torch brand zinc did not meet the exchange's quality standards had been withdrawn by the company involved.

"Recently one company made a possible quality claim to LME for LME registered Torch brand SHG zinc, but finally has withdrawn last week since, as a matter of fact they cannot find any quality problems," Zhuzhou said in a statement received here.
Earlier on Monday Japanese traders said rumours had been circulating in the Asian metals market that Swiss trader Glencore had requested the LME check the quality of Torch zinc.
Officials at Glencore metal offices around the region could not immediately be reached for comment on the issue.
The rumours helped helped zinc reach a new 6-3/4 year high in London on Friday.
Zhuzhou said the quality claim would not affect shipments of Torch branch zinc, which totalled 16,000 tonnes to the physical market and the LME warehouse in Singapore this month.
